title: Cognitive Workload and Psychomotor Vigilance Under Chronic Confinement
author: Cognitive Performance Laboratory
excerpt: Extended confinement causes subtle degradation in psychomotor vigilance response speed and working memory accuracy. High cognitive workload combined with acute stressors accelerates mental fatigue, leading to a compensatory surge in sympathetic arousal (elevated EDA and suppressed vagal HRV) despite static posture. Monitoring both subjective workload and objective telemetry prevents cognitive saturation.
